newsitem.title: USA: Conrail director says CSX offer was final.
newsitem.headline: Conrail director says CSX offer was final.

text.p: Conrail Inc board member Claude Brinegar told a federal court Thursday that CSX Corp indicated last month that its latest takeover bid for Conrail was its final offer.

As the Conrail board was considering the offer, Brinegar said, it received indications from Conrail Chairman David LeVan that "CSX had repeatedly stressed that this was their last offer...this was as far as they could go".
Rival bidder Norfolk Southern Corp, whose higher takeover offer has been spurned by Conrail, is challenging the proposed merger of Conrail and CSX.

Testifying before U.S. District Court Judge Donald Van Artsdalen, Brinegar also said a Conrail merger with Norfolk Southern would leave the surviving company with a high debt ratio and threaten its ability to weather an industry downturn.

"I have a worry that a railroad shouldn't take on too much debt," said Brinegar, who served as U.S. transportation secretary in the 1970s and engineered the formation of Conrail from several bankrupt northeastern railroads.
"I'd hate to re-run that, to even hint that that might happen," he said, referring to previous railroad collapses.
The latest revision in the terms of the proposed Conrail-CSX merger includes an offer valued at $16 a share for Conrail's convertible preferred stock.

Brinegar said the Conrail board had sought $20 for the shares, but CSX balked. The Conrail board then accepted the $16 offer, deciding that a rejection of the CSX bid could leave it without a partner.
"The risk of having no deal worried the directors quite a bit," Brinegar said.
The hearing was expected to last until early afternoon.
